title: Indian Polity Test 2 (Governance, Rights & Bodies — most probable)

questions.q: Panchayati Raj institutions got constitutional status through the:
questions.explain: The 73rd Amendment covers rural local bodies (Panchayats); the 74th covers urban bodies (Municipalities).

questions.q: The 74th Amendment Act, 1992 deals with:
questions.explain: Rural = 73rd, Urban = 74th — the pair is asked every exam cycle.

questions.q: The Gram Sabha in a village consists of:
options: All registered voters of the village
questions.explain: The Gram Sabha is the assembly of all voters of the village and is the foundation of Panchayati Raj.

questions.q: What minimum share of seats is constitutionally reserved for women in Panchayats?
questions.explain: The Constitution mandates at least one-third reservation for women; many states have raised it to one-half by law.

questions.q: The Anti-Defection Law is contained in the:
questions.explain: Added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985, it disqualifies legislators who defect from their party.

questions.q: The voting age in India was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the:
questions.explain: The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age for Lok Sabha and Assembly elections to 18.

questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced by the:
questions.explain: Goods and Services Tax (GST) was rolled out on 1 July 2017 after the 101st Amendment created the GST Council (Article 279A).

questions.q: The Nari Shakti Vandan Act (women's reservation in legislatures) is the:
questions.explain: It reserves one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, to apply after delimitation.

questions.q: National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog, which replaced the Planning Commission, is a/an:
options: Statutory body under an Act of Parliament
questions.explain: National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog was created by a cabinet resolution (1 Jan 2015) — unlike Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) or the Election Commission, it is not in the Constitution.

questions.q: Who is the Chairperson of National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog?
questions.explain: Like the old Planning Commission, National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog is chaired by the Prime Minister (PM); it has a Vice-Chairperson and a Chief Executive Officer (CEO).

questions.q: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office:
options: By a simple majority of Lok Sabha
In the same manner as a Supreme Court judge
questions.explain: This protection keeps the Election Commission independent of the ruling government.

questions.q: After the 44th Amendment, the Right to Property is a legal right under Article:
questions.explain: Article 31 and 19(1)(f) were deleted; property became a constitutional/legal right under Article 300A.

questions.q: Fundamental Duties are listed in Article:
questions.explain: Part IV-A has one Article, 51A, listing the duties — originally 10, now 11 after the 86th Amendment added a duty for parents/guardians.

questions.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in:
questions.explain: DPSPs (Part IV) guide the government but cannot be enforced by courts; Fundamental Rights are in Part III.

questions.q: Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.explain: Part III (Articles 12-35) is called the Magna Carta of India.

questions.q: The ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity in the Preamble were inspired by the:
questions.explain: Justice, in contrast, draws on the Russian Revolution's ideals, and the Preamble's structure on several sources.

questions.q: In the Indian context, 'secular' means the State:
options: Treats all religions equally and has no religion of its own
questions.explain: Indian secularism is equal respect for all religions (sarva dharma samabhava), unlike strict separation in the West.

questions.q: National Emergency can be proclaimed by the President under Article:
questions.explain: 352 = National Emergency (war, external aggression, armed rebellion); 356 = President's Rule; 360 = Financial Emergency.

questions.q: President's Rule in a State is imposed under Article:
questions.explain: Article 356 applies when a State's constitutional machinery fails; it is the most frequently used emergency provision.

questions.q: Financial Emergency is provided for in Article:
questions.explain: A Financial Emergency under Article 360 has never been proclaimed in India so far.

questions.q: How many times has National Emergency been proclaimed in India?
questions.explain: 1962 (China war), 1971 (Pakistan war) and 1975 (internal disturbance) — the 1975 one is the most debated.

questions.q: Panchayati Raj in India has a structure of:
questions.explain: Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block) and Zila Parishad (district) are the three tiers.

questions.q: The head of a Municipal Corporation is called the:
questions.explain: The Mayor is the elected head; the Municipal Commissioner is the chief executive officer appointed by the state government.

questions.q: The Lokpal is a body created to:
options: Inquire into corruption complaints against public functionaries
questions.explain: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 created the Lokpal at the Centre and Lokayuktas in states.

questions.q: The Right to Information (RTI) Act, which empowers citizens to seek information from public authorities, was passed in:
questions.explain: The Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005 replaced the weaker Freedom of Information Act and is a major transparency tool.

questions.q: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established in:
questions.explain: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.q: State Legislative Councils (Vidhan Parishad) can be created or abolished under Article:
questions.explain: Parliament can create/abolish a Legislative Council if the State Assembly passes a resolution by special majority.

questions.q: How many States in India presently have a bicameral legislature (with a Legislative Council)?
questions.explain: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh have Legislative Councils.

questions.q: The Public Accounts Committee of Parliament consists of members from:
options: Both Lok Sabha (15) and Rajya Sabha (7)
questions.explain: Its 22 members examine government spending; by convention its chairman is from the Opposition.

questions.q: The largest committee of Parliament, the Estimates Committee, has members only from the:
questions.explain: The Estimates Committee (30 members, all from Lok Sabha) suggests economies in government expenditure.

questions.q: 'Zero Hour' in Parliament, a period for raising urgent matters without notice, is:
questions.explain: Zero Hour begins at 12 noon after Question Hour; it is not mentioned in the Rules or the Constitution.

questions.q: A motion of no-confidence against the Council of Ministers can be moved only in the:
questions.explain: Since the ministry is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, only it can remove the government.

questions.q: The Chief Minister of a State is appointed by the:
options: Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.explain: The Governor appoints the leader of the majority party/coalition as Chief Minister (Article 164).

questions.q: The highest law officer of a State is the:
questions.explain: The Advocate General advises the State Government (Article 165); the Attorney General is the Union counterpart.

questions.q: The Inter-State Council, which discusses matters of common interest between States, is set up under Article:
questions.explain: Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council; it was first set up in 1990.

questions.q: The oath of office to the Governor of a State is administered by the:
options: Chief Justice of the State High Court
questions.explain: The Governor is sworn in by the High Court's Chief Justice (or senior-most judge available).

questions.q: Which of the following is a constitutional body?
options: National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog
questions.explain: Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is created by Article 315 of the Constitution; National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog is an executive-resolution body.

questions.q: Question Hour in Parliament is generally the:
questions.explain: Members ask starred, unstarred and short-notice questions during the first hour.

questions.q: The concept of 'Judicial Review' — courts striking down laws that violate the Constitution — was borrowed from:
questions.explain: Judicial review, along with Fundamental Rights and impeachment, came from the American Constitution.

questions.q: The procedure for the election of the President of India was borrowed from:
questions.explain: Ireland also gave India the DPSPs and the nomination of Rajya Sabha members from literature, art, science and social service.
